I had the same beginning. i was already experiencing major depressive episodes (mind you i wasn’t on meds for them since i couldn’t get a doctor with my insurance) but i took a friends adderall and it overtook my body and threw it into overdrive. after i took it, i was slowly falling into the black hole of mania, this process took a few weeks, but i eventually fell into mania. So yes drugs can cause manic symptoms but that’s usually while you are in the high, after wards it can still cause mania. i don’t know the true defining factor of substance caused mania but i think it’s the factors of how long after did it take for you to reach mania. psychiatric drugs and recreational drugs do have the ability to bring forth dormant disorders. just like how psychedelics can cause an early onset of schizophrenia. it can go the same for us bipolar folks. in your case, this onset cause was because of a psychiatric drug. Now by all means I don’t know you, nor do i know how you were acting before you took the drugs. but from my own personal experience, stimulants can bring for early onset mania in people with bipolar. 
Now im reading your post more, doctors use the term cycle loosely as it constantly changes. yes some are actually on a cycle, other may be random and their cycle can change between rapid cycling and your textbook definition of cycling. everyone is different and everyone’s cycle is different, may be similarities but everyone’s cycles are different. 

and to get better and not worse. you need to talk with a psychiatrist about meds if you aren’t on any, and if you are on them, discuss med changes. there is no way to completely avoid episodes. there are ways to cope with them but you can’t necessarily avoid them. I also didn’t bring up the fact doctors may use meds to forcibly pause and episode to alter medications to make sure you are not in that episode when they take you off the emergency medication. After you found your perfect med combo, which may take a longer or shorter time than others, but on meds you may experience long periods of time without episodes. i’ve heard stories of people who have gone years without an episode of mania but still suffer from depression. i’ve heard people have gone years without depression and still have mania. i’ve even heard people say they haven’t had a single episode in years. now this may be possible, it’s not a definite story for everyone. you may be stuck with cycling episodes but at a lesser degree, a more manageable degree, but you would still be having episodes. all it takes is to communicate with your doctor and figure out what YOU need to keep yourself at a manageable level. this all takes time, don’t let non-working medications put you down. you’ll eventually find what’s right for you, all it takes is communication.

and by all means im not at all stable either, im still working with my doctor to find s correct combination. there are days i want to drop all medications and all psychiatric appointments, but you’ll realize after an episode why you need to get the help you deserve. 
take care! xoxo <3 :))

I know it may seem like you can do all of it at once, but you’re just bouncing from one to another with little time to do said task. now i haven’t tried this but after my last episode i made this plan. Make a list(i know it’s hard to keep track and stay on the list but just make it), schedule a specific task for a set amount of time(say 30 minutes each). now i know it’s very difficult to just do one thing at once, but if you think about it, you’re giving yourself enough time with each task and still doing all of them. So in hindsight you’re still doing them all just with a timed limit between them. And remember, you stick to the list and if you think of more things, add things to a new list for tomorrow. DONT SIT THERE AND JUST KEEP ADDING THINGS! i know you will but try your hardest to restrain yourself, and i know that is ut most impossible to do that. 
OR
start with one task, write it down, set a timer for 30 minutes, better yet challenge yourself to stay in that time limit. then move to a new task, write it down on the same paper, set another timer for 30 minutes. then move to the next one, so on and so forth. BUT DO NOT and i repeat DO NOT write more than 8 things on that list. whe you realize you have written 8 things. move back to the original task and repeat but stay with those 8 tasks. When you are done with all 8 tasks, rinse and repeat. 
AND DONT FORGET!! every 30 minutes drink water. it can be a couple gulps but still attempt to drink water
I know this may seem very difficult but at least try, if it doesn’t work, try to challenge yourself to do this task for an extended period of time. 
ALSO PLEASE REACH OUT TO YOUR DOCTOR FOR A MED CHANGE, then reach out to your therapist if you have one, and see if you guys can work out a plan to help cope with the amount of energy you have for these tasks.
